cards.text: Zechariah, a prophet of the LORD, has a new message, and he calls it a burden. It's aimed at the land of Hadrach and at Damascus, its resting place. And while it goes out, the eyes of men and of all the tribes of Israel are fixed on somebody.

cards.question: While this burden goes out against Hadrach and Damascus, who are the eyes of men and of all the tribes of Israel fixed on?

cards.text: The burden keeps rolling to Hamath, which borders it, and then on to Tyre and Sidon. Friend, this message has more stops than a delivery truck.

cards.question: Zechariah's burden describes Tyre and Sidon as very shrewd.

cards.text: Tyre has built herself a fortress and heaped up silver like dust and gold like the dirt of the streets. Friend, I spent YEARS in a junk drawer counting dust, and not one speck of it was silver.

cards.question: Tyre has her fortress and her piles of silver and gold. What will the Lord do with all that wealth?
Tyre's fortress will keep her safe from fire.

cards.text: Next on the list are Ashkelon, Gaza and Ekron. First up, Ashkelon will see.

cards.question: When Ashkelon sees, it will celebrate.

cards.text: Ashkelon will fear. Gaza will writhe in agony, and so will Ekron, because her hope will wither.

cards.question: There will no longer be a ___ in Gaza, and Ashkelon will be left with no one living there.

cards.text: A mixed race will move into Ashdod. Then the LORD says it straight: "I will cut off the pride of the Philistines."
And then... the twist nobody saw coming. The LORD says He'll remove the blood from their mouths and the abominations from between their teeth.

cards.question: Once the LORD removes the blood and the abominations from the Philistines' mouths, what will they become?

answers.text: Servants of the city of Tyre

cards.question: The Philistines will become like a clan in ___.

cards.text: Even Ekron will be like the Jebusites. One minute they're on the burden list, the next minute they've got a name tag that says COUSIN.

cards.question: With an army marching to and fro, the LORD says He'll camp around His ___.
The LORD says never again will an oppressor overrun His people. Why not?

answers.text: He keeps watch with His own eyes
Their walls will be too high
Their army will be too strong

cards.text: Now the whole mood changes. A call goes out to the Daughter of Zion and the Daughter of Jerusalem, because somebody's on the way.

cards.question: Somebody's coming to Zion. What are the Daughter of Zion and the Daughter of Jerusalem told to do?

answers.text: Rejoice greatly and shout in triumph
Mourn and sit down in silence
Run and hide up in the hills

cards.text: Why all the shouting? Their King is coming to them, righteous and victorious, and I'm already looking around for the trumpets.

cards.question: This righteous and victorious King coming to Zion is also described as humble.
A King who's righteous, victorious and humble is coming to Zion. What's He riding?

cards.text: A DONKEY. I had the trumpets lined up, and the King comes humble, on a colt, the foal of a donkey.
Hold onto that donkey, friend. The Gospel of Matthew says this was fulfilled when Jesus rode into Jerusalem (Matthew 21:4-10).
Then the LORD says He'll cut off the chariot from Ephraim and the horse from Jerusalem, and the bow of war will be broken.

cards.question: With the chariot cut off and the bow of war broken, the King will proclaim ___ to the nations.
The King's dominion will stop at the borders of Jerusalem.

cards.text: Now the LORD turns to His people, and some of them are prisoners in a waterless pit. Friend, I know a little about being stuck in the dark, waiting for somebody to open things up.

cards.question: What will the LORD do for His people's prisoners in the waterless pit?
The LORD will set the prisoners free because of the blood of His ___.

cards.text: Then He tells them to return to their stronghold and calls them prisoners of hope. That's the expired coupon I shared a drawer with, friend: way past its date and STILL believing.

cards.question: Even today, the LORD declares He'll restore to the prisoners of hope ___.

cards.text: Then the picture turns to battle, and the LORD needs a bow.

cards.question: The battle's coming. What does the LORD say He'll bend as His bow?

cards.text: Judah's the bow, and He'll fit it with Ephraim. Then He'll rouse the sons of Zion against the sons of another nation.

cards.question: The LORD will rouse the sons of Zion against the sons of Egypt.

cards.text: It's the sons of Greece, and the LORD will make Zion like the sword of a mighty man. Then the LORD will appear over them.

cards.question: When the LORD appears over His people, His arrow will go forth like ___.

cards.text: The Lord GOD will sound the ram's horn and advance in the whirlwinds of the south. Friend, I JUMP when the oven timer goes off, so a ram's horn and a whirlwind would send me face-first into the chocolate chips, base and all.

cards.question: With the ram's horn sounding, who will shield the people in the battle?

cards.text: They'll destroy and conquer with slingstones, and they'll drink and roar as with wine.

cards.question: The LORD's people will be ___ like sprinkling bowls, drenched like the corners of the altar.
On that day, the LORD their God will save His people. He'll save them as what?

cards.text: Like jewels in a crown, they will sparkle over His land. I bet Sparkle would be crying happy tears at this one.

cards.question: After all that, Zechariah's message ends with the LORD's people worn out and hungry.

cards.text: From prisoners in a waterless pit to jewels in a crown, friend. Grain will make the young men flourish, and new wine, the young women.

findings.problem: The card says the eyes of men and all the tribes of Israel are fixed on somebody 'while it goes out.' Zechariah 9:1 links the two with 'for' ('for the eyes of men and of all the tribes of Israel are upon the LORD'). Changing 'for' to 'while' replaces the connection the text gives with a different one. Card 2's question repeats the same 'While this burden goes out' framing.

rule.text: Retelling: Papa Dorin can retell in his own words and fill in what the text clearly implies. Scene-setting details are fine. He never says anything the text shows is wrong.

findings.problem: The card introduces Zechariah as a prophet of the LORD and cites only Zechariah 9:1. Zechariah is not named anywhere in 9:1-17. The fact comes from outside the passage (Zechariah 1:1) and carries no reference.

rule.text: Facts from outside the passage are fine when they help, like who a new person is or who wrote a letter, with their reference.

findings.problem: No story card sets up verse 8. The blank asks the baker to guess the exact word 'house' against 'gates' and 'fields.' All three are things the LORD could camp around, so nothing earlier lets the baker reason it out. This tests wording the baker hasn't seen.

rule.text: The rule against guessing the next words of a line (see below) applies to every passage, and to fill in the blank too. The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.

findings.problem: This story card tells no part of Zechariah 9. It only points to Matthew 21:4-10. It still cites Zechariah 9:9, a verse that card 6 has already told. The fulfillment line would need to ride on a card that also tells part of the passage.

rule.text: Every story card tells part of the passage. Jokes ride along on those cards.

findings.problem: The card carries three beats. It reveals the sons of Greece, says Zion will be made like the sword of a mighty man, and says the LORD will appear over them.

rule.text: Aim for one beat per story card. Two is the most. If a story card has more than two things happening, split it.

findings.problem: The question includes 'drenched like the corners of the altar' right beside the blank. That rules out 'emptied' and 'broken' at once and leaves only 'filled.'

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: The statement says 'Zechariah's message ends' with verse 17. The burden that begins in 9:1 continues into chapter 10 (Zechariah 10:1). Framing verse 17 as the end of his message isn't true.

rule.text: What he points out must be true.
